description:
Found by the fz-kdt.199 build (2026-09-03) the hard way -- it destroyed three
corpus fixtures mid-run before the signature was recognised.

`--log-telemetry` takes a path. Written AFTER the subcommand, as in

    fz2 interp --log-telemetry fixtures2/behavior/some_fixture.fz

the parser binds the FIXTURE PATH as the log target, opens it for writing, and
truncates it to zero. The program then has no source to compile, so the symptom
is a "stall" or an empty-source error that REPRODUCES AT BASE -- exactly the
fz-go4.18.40 signature (an empty fixture -> undefined root -> deterministic
stall) that has already cost this project one long misdiagnosis. The user`s own
source file is destroyed in the process; only `git checkout` recovers it, and
only if the file is tracked and unmodified.

This is a destructive default. A flag that names an OUTPUT path must never
silently accept, and truncate, a path that was meant as an input. Options, in
order of preference: refuse to open a log target that already exists unless an
explicit overwrite flag is given; refuse a log target whose extension is `.fz`;
require the flag before the subcommand and diagnose it after; or at minimum
open the log O_EXCL and report the collision.

REPRODUCER (on a COPY -- this deletes the file):
    cp fixtures2/00002_types_top_level.fz /tmp/victim.fz
    fz2 interp --log-telemetry /tmp/victim.fz
    wc -c /tmp/victim.fz     # 0

CONCORDANT: fz-go4.18.40 / fz-go4.18.42 (both closed) are the prior art on
"a truncated fixture masquerades as nondeterminism"; the memory note from that
saga says to check `wc -c` on the fixture FIRST. This ticket removes the way
the truncation happens in the first place.

RED-FIRST: the command above leaves /tmp/victim.fz byte-identical and reports a
usage error naming the flag.
title: [BUG] `interp --log-telemetry <fixture>` silently TRUNCATES the fixture: a misplaced flag makes the source file the log target
